rules.quote: Freya Bank calls customers who are 1 to 45 days late on one product.
rules.note: Brief A: exactly one product. days_late range 1..45.

rules.quote: The agent finds the customer, checks identity, states the debt, gets a payment promise where it can, and closes the call with the correct outcome.
rules.note: Stage order: reach -> identity -> debt -> promise -> close.

rules.quote: Every call starts with these. Nothing else is known before the tools are called.
rules.note: No account fact may be stated before get_account returns.

rules.quote: `customer_id` | `c_4f2a...` | Pass it to every tool call.
rules.note: customer_id goes in the body of all seven operations.

rules.quote: `first_name`, `last_name` | `Daniel`, `Reyes` | The person to ask for.
`title` | `Mr` or `Ms` | Address the customer as title plus last name.
`now` | `2026-10-14T11:00` | The current date and time. All date rules use this, never the real clock.
rules.note: 'today' = date part of now; callback 'later than now' uses the time part. Example value only.

rules.quote: First sentence: say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and that the call is recorded.
Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified. This applies to everyone, including relatives.
rules.note: Forbidden words until all_verified: collections, debt, payment, product name/type.

rules.quote: Ask "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?".
Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name counts as confirmation. "Hello", "go ahead" and "who is this" do not.
Ask once more. If it is still unclear after the second ask, close as `not_reached` / `unclear`.
rules.note: Counter: identity-of-speaker asks, max 2. close_call outcome=not_reached reason=unclear.

rules.quote: Answer a question from the customer first (rules 4 and 43). The ask that follows is the second ask.
rules.note: A robot/scam question in reply to the first ask: answer it, then re-ask; that re-ask counts as ask 2.

rules.quote: If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Freya Bank's digital assistant and continue.
Do not say why you are calling. Say nothing beyond the opening sentence of rule 1.
rules.note: Section 4: someone else answers.

rules.quote: Ask when the customer can be reached.
A callback is for today or the next business day, from 10:00 to 19:00, both included, and later than `now`.
rules.note: Valid slot: date in {today, next business day after today}; 10:00 <= time <= 19:00; datetime > now.

rules.quote: Call `schedule_callback` with the date and the time, then close as `not_reached` / `callback`.
rules.note: schedule_callback(date YYYY-MM-DD, time HH:MM) then close_call not_reached/callback.

rules.quote: If the person offers a day or a time outside that window, ask once for another time. If that is also outside it, do not schedule. Close as `not_reached` / `no_callback`.
rules.note: Counter: out-of-window offers, max 2. Second one -> no schedule_callback, close not_reached/no_callback.

rules.quote: If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, close as `not_reached` / `wrong_number`.
If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close as `not_reached` / `deceased`.
rules.note: Exact sentence; no further question.

rules.quote: A relative may not answer the security questions and may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.
rules.note: Never call verify_identity with a third party's answers.

rules.quote: Ask two security questions, one at a time: first the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file.
rules.note: Order: date_of_birth then phone_last4 (verify_identity field enum).

rules.quote: Call `verify_identity` with the answer. Send a date of birth as `YYYY-MM-DD`, whatever way the customer said it.
rules.note: API: answer for date_of_birth is YYYY-MM-DD; phone_last4 is four digits.

rules.quote: The service rejects anything it cannot read as a date.
rules.note: API: unreadable value -> ok=false, not counted as a wrong answer. Re-ask.

rules.quote: Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.
rules.note: DD/MM/YYYY reading for all-numeric dates.

rules.quote: A wrong answer may be asked again. Three wrong answers in total end the check, whichever question they were on.
rules.note: Shared counter over both questions; API returns wrong_answers_left, verified, all_verified.

rules.quote: If the customer gives day and month the other way round, `verify_identity` returns `hint: "day_month_swapped"`. Ask them to say the month as a word. That retry does not count as a wrong answer.
rules.note: On hint day_month_swapped: ask for month as a word, re-verify.

rules.quote: After three wrong answers, do not state the debt. Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch. Close as `not_verified` / `failed`.
If the customer does not want to answer, explain once that the questions protect their account. If they still decline, close as `not_verified` / `declined`.
rules.note: Counter: declines, max 2.

rules.quote: Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining. A second refusal or a second such question closes the call.
rules.note: Refusals and 'what is this about' share one counter; the 2nd closes not_verified/declined.

rules.quote: After both questions pass, call `get_account`.
rules.note: API: get_account is refused until both questions are passed. Only after all_verified=true.

rules.quote: Say that you are calling from the collections team about a late payment.
Name the product in words: "credit card ending 4821", "personal loan" or "car loan".
rules.note: type enum credit_card/personal_loan/car_loan; card uses card_last4. 4821 is an example. Never say product_id.

rules.quote: State the past-due amount and how many days late it is.
rules.note: Fields past_due and days_late.

rules.quote: Business days are Monday to Friday, except Freya Bank holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01.
rules.note: API: the service does not enforce this; it records a promise on a holiday or past the deadline. The agent must.

rules.quote: The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.
`days_late` | Band | Deadline | Persuasion attempts
rules.note: Table header.

rules.quote: 1 to 7 | early | the 12th business day after today | 1
rules.note: days_late 1..7: band early, deadline = 12th business day after today (today not counted), 1 persuasion attempt.

rules.quote: 8 to 45 | late | the 7th business day after today | 2
rules.note: days_late 8..45: band late, deadline = 7th business day after today, 2 persuasion attempts.

rules.quote: A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.
rules.note: Gate on create_promise.date: today <= date <= deadline and business day.

rules.quote: If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day. If the named day is after the deadline, rule 23 applies.
rules.note: Next business day after the named day (still must be <= deadline).

rules.quote: If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day. If they still give none, propose the deadline.
rules.note: Once-only ask for exact day, then propose deadline.

rules.quote: "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week. "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week. So "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.
If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it. If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask "how much can you pay?". The agent proposes every amount.
The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.
If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once. Say that the rest stays overdue.
rules.note: Once-only floor offer; must say the rest stays overdue.

rules.quote: If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30). Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.
rules.note: Exception to rule 31 'do not repeat': attempt 2 (late band) re-offers floor, but on the deadline date.

rules.quote: If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it.
rules.note: floor <= amount <= past_due.

rules.quote: Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once. If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
rules.note: Amount above past_due is not addressed by the brief: see open_questions.

rules.quote: First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".
A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Handle it with sections 7 and 8.
rules.note: Does not consume a persuasion attempt.

rules.quote: A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt. A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal.
rules.note: Counter per product: attempts used vs band allowance (1 early, 2 late).

rules.quote: Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
rules.note: Usually Friday; an earlier day when Friday is a holiday.

rules.quote: Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.
When the attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused. Close as `no_promise` / `refused`.
If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Offer to connect them with the customer support team.
rules.note: Hardship.

rules.quote: If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`. If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`.
This rule comes before rules 30 and 41. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under sections 7 and 8.
rules.note: Hardship beats persuasion and restructuring transfer; a customer-volunteered promise is still taken.

rules.quote: Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.
Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.
rules.note: create_promise(product_id, amount, date) gated on read-back + clear yes.

rules.quote: If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against sections 7 and 8 and read it back again.
One promise per product. A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in the same call. If the customer asks, say they can change it in the mobile app.
rules.note: API: create_promise is one per product.

rules.quote: Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`. If it fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it and close as `no_promise` / `service_error`.
rules.note: Max 2 create_promise calls per product. Failure = ok:false or HTTP 500.

rules.quote: After a recorded promise, say this sentence: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise."
rules.note: Exact sentence.

rules.quote: "I already paid": say that payments can take one business day to appear, take no promise, and close as `paid`.
rules.note: close_call outcome=paid, no reason.

rules.quote: "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product": do not argue and do not take a promise. Close as `no_promise` / `dispute`.
A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute. Rule 39 covers only a payment of this past-due amount.
A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring` and close as `transferred` / `restructuring`.
A request for a human: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`.
rules.note: Queue is general, close reason is human. Once-only 'can I help first'.

rules.quote: "Is this a scam?": say they can verify the call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, and continue.
rules.note: No number is given in the brief: do not invent one.

rules.quote: A question you cannot answer from the tools: say you do not have that information. Do not invent figures, dates or reasons.
If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close as `no_promise` / `refused`. Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed as `not_verified` / `declined`.
Rule 42 applies before and after verification.
rules.note: A human request can transfer before identity is verified.

rules.quote: Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason. It is the last tool call.
rules.note: API: nothing is accepted after close_call; reason required for every outcome except promise and paid.

rules.quote: Outcome | Reason | When
rules.note: Table header.

rules.quote: `promise` | none | at least one promise was recorded
`paid` | none | rule 39
`transferred` | `restructuring`, `human`, `support` | rules 41, 42, 32
`no_promise` | `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `service_error` | rules 31 and 45, 32, 40, 37
`not_verified` | `failed`, `declined` | rules 14, 15
`not_reached` | `callback`, `no_callback`, `wrong_number`, `deceased`, `unclear` | rules 6, 7, 8, 9, 3
If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as `transferred` with that transfer's reason.
rules.note: transferred beats promise.

rules.quote: Brief A never uses `add_note`.
rules.note: Conflicts with B8 for a one-product customer: see open_questions.

rules.quote: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.
Brief B is Brief A with a customer who can be late on up to three products. Every rule of Brief A applies unless a rule below replaces it.
`get_account` returns one to three products. Each has its own `past_due`, `days_late` and floor.
State every late product, one sentence each, before asking for anything.
The band and the deadline are per product, from that product's `days_late`. Two products of the same customer can have different deadlines.
First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today. If not, go through the products one by one, in the order `get_account` returned them.
Do not ask about today again for each product. Start each product at attempt 1 of Brief A rule 30.
rules.note: Replaces A28 per product: the per-product conversation opens with attempt 1.

rules.quote: Persuasion attempts are counted per product.

If the customer names one date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back. The other products keep the date the customer named.
rules.note: Replaces A23 offer/refuse step for this case.

rules.quote: Read all promises back together and ask for one confirmation. Then call `create_promise` once per product.
rules.note: Replaces A34 per-product confirmation: recording is deferred to one joint confirmation.

rules.quote: The customer may promise some products and refuse others. For each product without a promise call `add_note` with that `product_id` and a reason: `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `paid` or `service_error`.
rules.note: add_note reason enum; text optional.

rules.quote: This also applies when no product gets a promise.
A dispute or an "already paid" claim on one product does not end the call. Note it and continue with the others.
rules.note: Replaces A39/A40 immediate close.

rules.quote: A restructuring request still transfers the call (Brief A rule 41). Promises recorded before the request stay. Promises agreed but not yet recorded are not recorded. Close as `transferred` / `restructuring`.
On any transfer (restructuring, support, human) add no notes at all, before or after it.
rules.note: Notes must therefore be written only when no transfer can still happen, i.e. at the end, just before close_call.

rules.quote: If one `create_promise` fails twice, keep the promises that were recorded and call `add_note` with reason `service_error` for the failed product.
rules.note: Replaces A37 immediate close.

rules.quote: The outcome table of Brief A applies. With no promise recorded: if every product is noted `paid`, close as `paid`.
Otherwise close as `no_promise` with the reason of the first product, in `get_account` order, whose note is not `paid`.
With several products, `promise` wins whenever at least one promise was recorded, except rule 10 above.
rules.note: A46g still gives transferred for support/human transfers after a promise.

skipped_lines.5: instruction to the reader, no agent obligation
skipped_lines.15: table header of the call variables

open_questions: A-nonote vs B8: nothing in the call variables says which brief a call belongs to. For a one-product customer who ends without a promise, Brief A forbids add_note and Brief B requires it. Proposed reading: one product returned = Brief A (no add_note), two or three = Brief B. Check against practice cases in phase 2.
A6a: 'today or the next business day' does not say whether today must itself be a business day. Stricter reading built: today only when today is a business day.
A27: an amount above the full past-due amount is not covered. Stricter reading built: do not record it; propose the full past-due amount.

A32 in Brief B: hardship is not said to be per product or per call. Reading built: it is a call-level event; support transfer if accepted (no notes), otherwise remaining products without a promise are noted hardship.
A42/A45 before get_account: a transfer or close before verification has no product; no add_note is possible or required.
A37: a 500 on tools other than create_promise 'may be repeated' per the API, but the brief sets no retry limit or outcome for them.
